sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed (FLAG construct, L1). GFP/SEP-GluA3 (L3/L4, same junction) showed normal surface mobility by FRAP and was used to rescue Aβ-mediated synaptic depression in GluA3-KO neurons, indicating functional competence of the tagged receptor.
sites.rationale: Signal peptide spans residues 1–28 (computed landmarks); the mature extracellular domain begins at residue 29. Python verification confirms residue 28 = G and residue 29 = G. L1 explicitly states the FLAG tag follows the signal peptide, making this a validated exact-site insertion. The tag sits 526 residues from TM1 (residue 555), well clear of any TM boundary. L4 (same N-terminal junction, topology-derived) demonstrates the GFP-tagged construct participates in synaptic function assays in neurons, supporting surface_and_function classification. Full-length human GluA3 expressed in a membrane-anchored context with a FLAG epitope inserted immediately after the 28-residue signal peptide cleavage site, placing the tag at the N-terminus of the large extracellular domain (residues 29–554). Corroborated by PMC11867010 (L2/L3/L4), which reports GFP- and SEP-tagged rat GluA3 (flip isoform) used for surface FRAP imaging and Aβ-mediated synaptic depression assays in CA1 neurons; 'GFP-GluA3' naming and surface-display requirement place those tags at the same N-terminal junction by topology.

sources.claim: The GluA3 construct was tagged with a Flag epitope at the N terminus, immediately following the signal peptide.

literature_notes: L2, L3, and L4 (all PMC11867010) describe GFP- and SEP-tagged GluA3 constructs used for surface FRAP and synaptic assays. The 'GFP-GluA3' naming convention and the requirement for extracellular display (SEP is pH-sensitive and reports surface receptors) place these tags at the N-terminus after the signal peptide — the only extracellular terminus of this type-I receptor — converging on the same junction as L1 (insert_after_residue=28). Because all four ledger lines pin the same junction, this is one site, not multiple. The S885A and K887A mutations mentioned in L2 are point mutations in the intracellular C-tail (residues 845–894), not tag insertions, and do not qualify as other_positions. No ledger line supports any internal loop insertion or a second distinct extracellular site.
